newsitem.title: USA: House Speaker Gingrich re-elected easily in Georgia.
newsitem.headline: House Speaker Gingrich re-elected easily in Georgia.

text.p: House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich won re-election in his home district in Georgia on Tuesday, overcoming a Democratic challenge by millionaire cookie magnate Michael Coles by a comfortable margin.
The Georgia Republican defeated Coles by a margin of about 57 to 43 percent to clinch a widely expected victory in the state's 6th Congressional District, where about half the voters are Republican.
In 1994, the year Gingrich led the Republican Party to its first takeover of Congress in 40 years, he beat his Democratic rival Ben Jones by 18 points.
An elated Gingrich, savoring the prospect of his 10th term in Congress, told a room full of cheering supporters that the victory was due to their grass-roots campaigning.
"By George, with your help, we won a smashing victory," the speaker said.

"To have the kind of friends that we have, to have the kind of volunteers, to have the kind of people who put up a yard sign ... it was the people power that went out all over this district that made the difference."
Gingrich and Coles spent the final weeks of the campaign in a big money war of radio and television advertising and a relentless schedule of public appearances.

Coles, the 53-year-old chief executive of the American Cookie Co., sought to appeal to Republican voters who disliked Gingrich's confrontational style of politics by conveying a nonpartisan message based on low taxes, a balanced budget and environmental protection.
Coles, with an estimated fortune of $30 million, had been expected to give Gingrich a competitive election battle financed with his own money.
But the Democrat's $2.3 million campaign proved too small to match a Gingrich war chest of $3.6 million provided by Republican supporters from across the country.

Despite Gingrich's low ratings in national opinion polls, his popularity at home remained largely untarnished by the issues such as Medicare, House ethics allegations and the confrontational tenor of the 104th Congress.

His stature as House speaker, combined with the loyalty of local business and military constituencies, abortion opponents and advocates of school prayer, appeared to carry the day for the 53-year-old former history professor.
